findings.claim: enableSqlExpressions returns false on both branches and discards the FlagSqlExpressions value. The sqlExpressions toggle therefore has no effect, and QueryTypeSQL is always rejected with 'sqlExpressions is not implemented'. The flag registry (pkg/services/featuremgmt/registry.go:1083-1088), the docs (feature-toggles/index.md:187) and the frontend (public/app/features/expressions/types.ts:73) still advertise and offer the feature when the flag is on.
findings.evidence: Reasoned, with no failing run. The patch body is `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(...); if enabled { return false }; return false` (reader.go:194-200), and it is called at reader.go:129-132. Proposed red test (mattpocock, superpowers): call NewExpressionQueryReader(featuremgmt.WithFeatures(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)).ReadQuery with type 'sql' and assert no error. On the pinned code it fails with 'sqlExpressions is not implemented'. The contrary contract (always rejected) is also possible; see reason.
findings.reason: Raised by 4 seats. Normalised to Important: mattpocock, ponytail and superpowers say Important, open-code-review says Minor. There is no spec, so intent is ambiguous. If intent is flag-controlled, the red test asserts no error with the flag on. If intent is a permanent kill (the commit subject 'disable sql expressions'), the fix is a plain `return false` plus deprecating or hiding the toggle and the frontend option, and the red test asserts the toggle or option is gone. The intent must be settled before writing the red test.

findings.claim: The local variable `enabled` holds `!IsEnabledGlobally(FlagSqlExpressions)`, so its name says the opposite of its value.

findings.claim: The legacy parse path, used when FlagExpressionParser is off (the default), does not go through the new ReadQuery gate. It goes UnmarshalSQLCommand → NewSQLCommand → sql.TablesList, which fails on the stub RunCommands and returns errutil.BadRequest('sql-invalid-sql', 'error reading SQL command'). For the same input, users get a different error that says their SQL is invalid rather than that the feature is disabled. On this path the disable relies on stub behaviour instead of an explicit check.
findings.evidence: Reasoned by tracing nodes.go:123-161 → sql_command.go:30-35 → sql/parser.go:23-29. Proposed red test (superpowers): build a SQL node through buildCMDNode with the parser flag off and assert the same 'disabled' error that the ReadQuery path returns.
findings.reason: Raised by 4 seats. Normalised to Minor: both correctness seats rated it Minor, and SQL is still blocked on both paths. The impact is a misleading error, not a functional failure. mattpocock rated it Important, and ponytail raised it inside its Important finding. Ponytail suggests putting the single explicit check in shared code at the top of NewSQLCommand so both paths return the same error.
